newsitem.title: UK: Vulnerable Ldn gold fixes at fresh low since 1993.
newsitem.headline: Vulnerable Ldn gold fixes at fresh low since 1993.

text.p: Gold balanced just above important support in early European trading on Tuesday and dealers said market expectations leaned overwhelmingly towards losses.
But some said a small bounce from current levels -- now at 4-1/4 year lows -- might give the market a brief respite in the very near term.
"Most people are anticipating gold will come lower. But some people are saying there could be a small bounce from $333 to $337 this afternoon," a London-based dealer said.
Gold fixed at $333.60 an ounce, compared to $334.55 on Monday afternoon, a fresh low fixing since March 30, 1993.
Analysts noted a band of support in the $332-$333 area.
But they added that below that level gold had no technical underpinning and was vulnerable to a fall to the key $325.10 low from 1993 -- the lowest point for gold in the past 11 years.
"Gold has fallen to four-year lows and continues to look weak," said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston. "Below $332 there's nothing until $325.10."
As prices decline, gold producers will be tempted to hedge future production, speeding up the price decline, dealers said.
"Producers may start piling in before it gets too late," a dealer said. "It's getting very very risky."

A bout of borrowing gave further evidence that the market expected prices to decline. One month lease rates climbed to 1.42 percent on Tuesday morning compared to 1.18 on Monday. A week ago one-month rates were quoted at 1.00 percent.
"People are short and are starting to borrow on all periods up to one year, hoping to buy it back at lower levels. This does not bode well for gold," a dealer said.
By contrast to gold, the platinum group metals (PGMs) were slightly firmer.
The market was still waiting for news that long-delayed Russian exports were coming onto the market.
Platinum fixed at $434.00 an ounce, up $4 from the Monday afternoon fixing. Chartists said it had potential for a short-term upwards correction with first resistance at $440.00.
Palladium was slightly steadier, fixing at $194.00 against $192.00 previously.
Silver was also slightly weaker and analysts said it was vulnerable to the downside, with key support at $4.60 an ounce.
It was last indicated at $4.65/$4.67 an ounce, compared to $4.66/$4.68 at Monday's London close.
